To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) animal welfare science is a multidisciplinary subject; 2) it involves both common sense and cutting edge science; 3) it involves both the assessment of positive and negative states of well-being; and 4) it has a strong ethical component.

1) the well-being of animals can be assessed by a combination of common sense and scientific research; 2) the scientific assessment of animal well-being involves finding indicators of high levels of biological functioning, freedom from suffering, and positive experiences; 3) the tools available to assess well-being include measures of biological functioning and productivity, pathology and epidemiology, pre-pathological states, corroborative measures of fear and pain, abnormal behavior, expression and measurement of emotions, environmental choice and preference tests,

the assessment of animal well-being requires 1) the use of common-sense and science; 2) an assessment of the three broad criteria of biological functioning, suffering, and positive experiences; 3) the use of a mixture of approaches, including productivity, veterinary science, physiological science, and behavioral science; 4) the development of new approaches to studying motivation; 5) the need to consider values, economics, regulation, and alternative systems; and 6) a focus on research
